product: AI data-center memory. HBM4 (1-beta DRAM) is in high-volume shipments for a lead customer and qualifying with multiple end-customers; HBM4E (1-gamma) development is underway with a calendar-2027 volume target; 512GB DDR5 RDIMM demo 2026-09-15; LP5X SOCAMM2 and G9 PCIe Gen6 SSD (2026-06-24, SEC).
demand: Price and mix. FQ3-26 revenue $41.46B versus $23.86B in the prior quarter, up 73.7% QoQ, with GAAP gross margin 84.6% versus 74.4% (2026-06-24, SEC); Core Data Center and Mobile/Client gross margins were both 87%. HBM crowds out conventional DRAM, lifting ASPs.
pricing_power: A memory price rollover plus capacity additions. Micron guides FQ4-26 GAAP gross margin near 86% (2026-06-24, SEC), a cycle peak; new competitor capacity, a DRAM/HBM price rollover, or any break in supply discipline would compress margins quickly.
competition: Not yet at the leading edge. Chinese memory makers are the low-cost threat: CXMT is mass-producing its latest DRAM and planning NAND expansion, and YMTC competes in NAND (aggregator 2026-09-20); neither matches HBM4/HBM4E. Samsung and SK hynix are the leading-edge substitutes (slicast.com 2026-09-22).
market_strategy: CEO Sanjay Mehrotra, 2026-06-24 (SEC EX-99.1): 'We believe our multi-year Strategic Customer Agreements will significantly enhance the durability and predictability of Micron's strong financial performance.' The same release guides FQ4-26 revenue $50.0B +/- $1.0B, GAAP gross margin about 86%, and non-GAAP EPS $31.00 +/- $1.00.
bull: FQ3-26 revenue $41.46B (+73.7% QoQ), GAAP gross margin 84.6%, EPS $25.11 beat; FQ4-26 guide $50.0B/86% margin; HBM sold out into 2027; Baird and Citigroup raised targets 2026-09-28/23.
bear: FQ4-26 print due 2026-09-30 is unverified; 86% margin is a cycle peak; Wells Fargo lowered 1525->1400 on 2026-09-23; USITC 337-TA-1523 probe and CXMT/YMTC low-cost capacity threaten pricing.
falsifier: FQ4 FY2026 results on 2026-09-30: revenue below $49.0B, GAAP gross margin below about 86%, or non-GAAP EPS below $31.00 versus the 2026-06-24 guide.

web_bottleneck: Micron relieves the AI memory supply bottleneck: HBM crowding out conventional DRAM tightens DDR5. Its own constraint is capital and advanced-packaging capacity, with FQ3-26 net capex $7.1B and TTM capex $25.26B (2026-06-24, SEC; stockanalysis.com 2026-09-28).
web_who_benefits_next: Second-order wafer and materials suppliers. Micron will invest up to $3B into the US supply chain, supporting GlobalWafers' US wafer expansion (2026-07-09, investors.micron.com); Boise and NY fab plus the $10B research buildout; server ecosystem enablers receiving DDR5 RDIMM samples (2026-06-24, SEC).
web_who_loses: Handset and PC OEMs absorbing memory cost inflation; server makers and Netlist respondents in USITC 337-TA-1523, namely Micron, HPE, Lenovo and Super Micro (2026-09-23, usitc.gov). Samsung and SK hynix lose share where Micron qualifies for NVIDIA Rubin (slicast.com 2026-09-22).

Samsung and SK hynix are the leading-edge substitutes (slicast.com 2026-09-22).
web_ceo_promised: CEO Sanjay Mehrotra, 2026-06-24 (SEC EX-99.1): 'We believe our multi-year Strategic Customer Agreements will significantly enhance the durability and predictability of Micron's strong financial performance.' The same release guides FQ4-26 revenue $50.0B +/- $1.0B, GAAP gross margin about 86%, and non-GAAP EPS $31.00 +/- $1.00.
web_did_they_deliver: So far yes. FQ3-26 (2026-06-24, SEC) revenue $41.46B, GAAP gross margin 84.6%, non-GAAP EPS $25.11, beating consensus $21.39 EPS and $35.91B revenue (MarketBeat 2026-09-21). FY2025 was a record (SEC 2025-09-23). The FQ4-26 promise is due 2026-09-30 and is still OPEN.
web_what_would_falsify: The FQ4 FY2026 print due 2026-09-30: revenue below $49.0B, GAAP gross margin below about 86%, or non-GAAP EPS below $31.00 versus the 2026-06-24 guide (SEC). Also a DRAM/HBM price rollover, or failure to hold the HBM4 design win for NVIDIA Rubin, where SK hynix already ships.
